analysis:
StandaloneServer.swift head 1964-1969 and 1999-2006: for GLM plans, the pre-load and post-load computeStandaloneWeightHash comparisons against manifest.aggregateSHA256 are removed. The pre-load call now passes required=false for GLM. Lines 2001-2003 use glmLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256, checked by ProviderLoop.requireGLM5NextLoadedArtifact, then copy it into preLoadArtifactHash. As a result, reusableSSDWeightHashDecision (2011) always returns .eligible for GLM. The cacheEligibleWeightHash that binds the SSD prefix cache (T-041 weightHash binding) now depends on the managed load hashing the same bytes it maps, a read-and-verify rather than a TOCTOU bracket. GLM5NextManagedLoad and requireGLM5NextLoadedArtifact are not in this batch. Integration should confirm that the verification covers the loaded bytes and fails closed on a nil hash. glmPlan.weights.recheck() is retained at 1969. Non-GLM bracketing is unchanged.
VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift (new) is an unauthenticated JSON hash cache with an environment-variable path override; see finding. Its callers (startup registration, record writers) are not supplied. Integration must check: whether a stored hash feeds the coordinator registration weight_hash; whether it can affect cacheEligibleWeightHash or modelArtifactSHA256; and whether record() is called only after full verification. weightsVerifiedByManagedLoad keys on modelType, the same predicate used for GLM managed-load gating at StandaloneServer 1804, so it is consistent.
StartupPreloader.swift: the new onFailure hook (head 91-93, 108-111, 197, 221) passes the raw error to GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice.report. It only logs operator-facing guidance; check that the notice prints no prompt data. No control-flow change was found there.

findings.detail: VerifiedWeightHashStore (lines 47-54, 79-86, 110-116) returns a stored aggregate SHA-256 as a verified hash when stat() identities match. The JSON at installDirectory/verified-weights.json, or any path named by DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE, has no MAC or signature. An operator (ADV-001) can write a record whose file identities match tampered weights and whose aggregateSHA256 is the catalog value. Device, inode, size, mtime and ctime are all read from the operator-controlled filesystem. A startup registration path that consults this store would then report a manifest-matching weight hash without reading the bytes. Before this PR, the attested process had to hash the weights itself to produce that claim (T-012/T-027/T-034). The doc comment (lines 12-15) says the managed GLM load re-verifies before serving, so the expected impact is a false registration and routing claim plus load-time failure, not unverified bytes in service. That guarantee depends on callers outside this batch. Plausible trigger: edit verified-weights.json or set the env override, then restart. Fix: authenticate records with a key derived from the SE-rooted KEK, ignore the environment override in release builds, or never surface stored hashes as attested registration evidence. Also update T-027/T-012 to describe the cached claim.
findings.title: Registration weight hash can come from an unauthenticated, operator-writable cache file
